authorship: New manually authored fictional utterances embedded in scripts/build_all_question_dataset.py.
split_assignment: Fixed at authorship; no randomized row-level split or paraphrase transformations. Groups are split-scoped semantic families.
training_role: Fit TF-IDF vocabulary, Logistic Regression coefficients, and development choices using train.csv only.
calibration_role: Held out from fitting; estimate split conformal quantiles after the model/configuration is fixed. Do not use to tune hyperparameters.
test_role: Reserved held-out authored evaluation; read once after implementation is fixed. Do not train or tune on evaluation outcomes.
context_assumption: Each row is interpreted under the exact current D-question wording and its stated hypothetical. No hidden previous answers are assumed.
label_policy: clarity proposes exactly one approved option pending confirmation; undecided and confusion have no option. D11 misconceptions are clarity candidates that require the deterministic understanding hold.
null_encoding: option_id is empty in CSV for null and JSON null in authoring metadata.
limitations: Synthetic-only data, created by one author; no real-customer, demographic, language, dialect or distributional representativeness claim.
Distinct split expressions and group IDs prevent direct overlap but cannot prove semantic independence; shared approved terminology is unavoidable.
Calibration has five clarity examples per option and ten examples per other intent per question. Sparse option coverage may produce broad or empty prediction sets.
TF-IDF models may fail on unseen numbers, negation, multiple clauses, ownership, temporal scope, currency or conditional meaning; these examples do not establish semantic understanding.
Conformal coverage relies on exchangeability; synthetic calibration does not imply coverage for real first-time investors.
Current specification remains marked business_review_draft_pending_user_and_mentor_review; this dataset is a prototype and requires independent label review.
No example confirms an answer or authorizes saving; deterministic safeguards, exact user confirmation and separate save consent remain necessary.
